_meta._comment: Keys beginning with an underscore are metadata, not repositories. Consumers must filter them out before iterating.

1.name: Core Platform & Board Contract
1.hint: Standard hardware driver engine and companion reference code.

2.name: Python Framebuffers & GUI Toolkits
2.hint: Zero external native dependencies — runs on any Python 3 host.

3.name: LVGL Native Extensions & Binding Generator
3.hint: Single-source LVGL C header binding generator and native interpreter modules.

4.name: App Hosts & Mobile
4.hint: Deploy PyDevices apps directly to desktop browsers or mobile APKs.

5.name: Developer Tools & Infrastructure
5.hint: MIP package indexing, multi-usermod builds, and serial/FTP IDE extensions.

excluded..github (dotgithub): No landing page by design. It holds org-wide data, scripts, and community health files, and is documented as markdown only.
excluded.android-runner: Exists solely to enable pydevices/bin/android.py. The APK is documented in pydevices; the runner publishes no site.

moved.displayif: now [`modules/displayif`](https://github.com/PyDevices/micropython-pydevices/tree/main/modules/displayif) in micropython-pydevices. The old repository is archived.
moved.audioif: now [`modules/audioif`](https://github.com/PyDevices/micropython-pydevices/tree/main/modules/audioif) in micropython-pydevices. The old repository is archived.
moved.cameraif: now [`modules/cameraif`](https://github.com/PyDevices/micropython-pydevices/tree/main/modules/cameraif) in micropython-pydevices. The old repository is archived.
moved.usbif: the C module is now [`modules/usbhost`](https://github.com/PyDevices/micropython-pydevices/tree/main/modules/usbhost) in micropython-pydevices; the Python USB packages are in [pydevices](https://github.com/PyDevices/pydevices/blob/main/docs/usb.md). The old repository is archived.

pydevices.headline: pydevices — Hardware Abstraction Layer & Core Contract.
pydevices.description: Unified pure-Python hardware abstraction layer and core device contract for MicroPython, CircuitPython, CPython, direct WebAssembly, Pyodide, and Android.

displayif.title: PyDevices - displayif (moved)
displayif.headline: displayif has moved into micropython-pydevices.
displayif.description: Moved to micropython-pydevices as modules/displayif, with its history. It was never published on its own: it reaches you in firmware built by micropython-pydevices' build_mp.py, so that is where it is built, tested and changed now. Your code doesn't change. The old repository is archived.

audiodsp.headline: audiodsp — CircuitPython-compatible audio for MicroPython and CPython.
audiodsp.description: CircuitPython's audio system (audiocore, synthio, audiomixer, effects, audiomp3) ported to MicroPython and CPython, extending CircuitPython along the way: dynamics, routing, convolution, and offline rendering. On PyPI as pydevices-audiodsp; the instrument and effect libraries built on it ship from audiocomponents.

audioif.title: PyDevices - audioif (moved)
audioif.headline: audioif has moved into micropython-pydevices.
audioif.description: Moved to micropython-pydevices as modules/audioif, with its history. It was never published on its own: it reaches you in firmware built by micropython-pydevices' build_mp.py, so that is where it is built, tested and changed now. Your code doesn't change. The old repository is archived.

audiocomponents.headline: audiocomponents — 55 classic instruments and 45 effects, in pure Python, on audiodsp.
audiocomponents.description: The instrument and effect libraries for audiodsp: audioinstruments (55 modelled classics, from the TR-808 to the DX7) and audioeffects (45 effect classes and racks), pure Python on MicroPython and CPython. Ships as pydevices-audioinstruments and pydevices-audioeffects, each a standalone distribution and a MIP package.

usbif.title: PyDevices - usbif (moved)
usbif.headline: usbif has moved, to two homes.
usbif.description: The C module is now usbhost, in micropython-pydevices as modules/usbhost (its binding is _usbhost, it was _usbif). The Python USB packages (usb.core, the host and device classes, usb-hid) are top-level packages in pydevices, installed with mip. Code that uses the packages doesn't change. The old repository is archived.

cameraif.title: PyDevices - cameraif (moved)
cameraif.headline: cameraif has moved into micropython-pydevices.
cameraif.description: Moved to micropython-pydevices as modules/cameraif, with its history. It was never published on its own: it reaches you in firmware built by micropython-pydevices' build_mp.py, so that is where it is built, tested and changed now. Your code doesn't change. The old repository is archived.

pygraphics.headline: pygraphics — 2D graphics engine & canvas framebuffer.
pygraphics.description: Native C and pure-Python 2D graphics library with drawing primitives, bitmap font rendering, paletted surface blitting, and area-dirtying pipelines.

pdwidgets.headline: pdwidgets — Pure-Python UI widget toolkit.
pdwidgets.description: Lightweight object-oriented UI widget framework including buttons, sliders, progress bars, labels, and event routing for PyDevices screens.

palettes.headline: palettes — Color math, wheels, cubes & swatch palettes.
palettes.description: Color management library with RGB565 / RGB888 output, an HSV color wheel, RGB color cubes, Material Design swatches, and Win16 color names.

lvgl-bindings.headline: lvgl-bindings — Automated C header parser & binding generator.
lvgl-bindings.description: Automated binding generator parsing LVGL C headers into native CPython extensions, MicroPython usermods, and CircuitPython modules.

lvgl-micropython.headline: lvgl-micropython — MicroPython C usermod for LVGL v9.
lvgl-micropython.description: Native MicroPython C module integrating LVGL v9 graphics engine with displayif bus drivers across ESP32, RP2040, and i.MX RT targets.

lvgl-python.headline: lvgl-python — CPython & Pyodide WASM extension wheels.
lvgl-python.description: Pre-built CPython extension wheels and Pyodide WASM packages bringing LVGL v9 to Linux, Windows, Android, and web browsers.

lvgl-circuitpython.headline: lvgl-circuitpython — CircuitPython native LVGL C module.
lvgl-circuitpython.description: CircuitPython native C module providing LVGL v9 bindings and displayif integration for Adafruit Feather and SAMD51 / RP2040 boards.

pyscript-template.headline: pyscript-template — Offline PWA starter template.
pyscript-template.description: Progressive Web App starter template repository for deploying offline-capable client-side PyDevices applications on GitHub Pages.

android-template.headline: android-template — Android APK Buildozer project.
android-template.description: Pre-configured python-for-android build recipes and Buildozer project template for packaging PyDevices applications into native Android APKs.

mpftp.headline: mpftp — board tools for the editor, CLI, and agents.
mpftp.description: Connect MicroPython and CircuitPython boards from VS Code, Cursor, or the CLI, over USB or Wi-Fi: dual-pane file transfer, in-editor REPL, firmware builds and flashing, mip/circup, plus RPC, MCP, and an optional browser PWA.

mip.headline: mip — PyDevices MIP package index & distribution.
mip.description: Single source of truth (SoT) for precompiled MicroPython .mpy bytecode packages and pure-Python library distributions across the PyDevices ecosystem.

pydevices-examples.headline: pydevices-examples — Showcase, demos & WebAssembly gallery.
pydevices-examples.description: Comprehensive example code, direct MicroPython WebAssembly demos, board configurations, and multi-interpreter showcase benchmarks.

pydevices-examples-gallery.title: pydevices-examples — WebAssembly Gallery
pydevices-examples-gallery.headline: WebAssembly Gallery
pydevices-examples-gallery.description: Direct MicroPython WebAssembly demos that run the same PyDevices examples as MCUs and CPython. Explore drawing, input, widgets, and LVGL without flashing a board first.
pydevices-examples-gallery.hero_note: Click a card to launch the app. The first load may take a few seconds while the interpreter downloads; featured demos stay pinned at the top.

pydevices-examples-pyscript.title: pydevices-examples — PyScript Gallery
pydevices-examples-pyscript.headline: PyScript Gallery
pydevices-examples-pyscript.description: Pyodide / PyScript demos that run full CPython in the browser — the same PyDevices examples as MCUs and the direct WebAssembly gallery. Explore drawing, input, widgets, and LVGL without flashing a board first.
pydevices-examples-pyscript.hero_note: Click a card to launch the app. The first load may take a few seconds while the interpreter downloads; featured demos stay pinned at the top.

PyDevices.github.io.headline: One display & hardware contract for MicroPython, CircuitPython, and CPython — from bare metal to the browser.
PyDevices.github.io.description: The same driver, event, and display code runs unmodified on bare-metal MicroPython and CircuitPython boards, as native CPython wheels on desktop and Android, and directly in a browser tab — no rewrites, no plugins.
PyDevices.github.io.hero_note: Get Started installs the Python packages, with pip on a desktop or mip on a board. To build MicroPython firmware with the modules compiled in, run curl -fsSL https://pydevices.github.io/install.sh | sh and follow the guide on the micropython-pydevices page.

micropython-pydevices.headline: micropython-pydevices — the versioned MicroPython runtime overlay.
micropython-pydevices.description: The PyDevices patch queue for MicroPython, kept like a distribution keeps one: an ordered, provenance-tracked patch series over the pinned upstream (MicroPython v1.30.0-preview-160), with presets, boards and variants that build PyDevices modules into firmware with upstream's own make.

workbench.headline: workbench — the browser IDE and MicroPython simulator.
workbench.description: A ViperIDE fork with a built-in WebAssembly MicroPython simulator: edit, run, and debug PyDevices code against a simulated board entirely in the browser, no hardware required.

mpvst.headline: MPVST — audio effects and instruments as a VST3 plug-in.
mpvst.description: Programmable VST3 instruments and effects: every audiocomponents instrument and effect as a named plug-in, each instance running its Python in a sidecar process. Installers for Windows and Linux; nothing has to be built.
